To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the single-channel conductances of LamB mutants with amino acid substitutions at the central constriction residue are increased as compared to that of the wild type, and that the magnitude of the increase depends on the size and charge of the introduced amino acid.

the single-channel conductances of LamB channels carrying the mutations Y118X (X = alanine, isoleine, serine, asparagin, cystein, aspartic, arginine, phenylalanin, and tryptphan) were increased by a factor of 1.6-6.2 as compared to wild-type channels and that the single-channel conductivity of the Y118D mutant was nonlinearly dependent on the concentration of the aqueous salt solution.
the mutation of the central constriction residue Y118 to a neutral, positively or negatively charged amino acid increases the single-channel conductances of the LamB channels by a factor of six.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the size and the charge of the side chain of Y118 on single-channel conductance of LamB.
the effect of size, charge, and hydrophobicity of amino acids on ion transport through the LamB channel.
the question of how the size and the charge of amino acids at the central constriction in the LamB channel influence single-channel conductance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the size of the amino acids inside the constriction of the pore is the most important determinant of single-channel conductance.
the size of an amino acid residue at the central constriction is the main determinant of the single-channel conductivity of LamB.
the central constriction is a very sensitive site in the LamB channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the single-channel conductances of the LamB mutants were mainly determined by the size of the amino acids in the central constriction, whereas the hydrophobicity and the charge of the amino acids had a minor effect.
the single-channel conductances of all LamB mutants were higher than those of wild-type LamB.
the single-channel conductances of LamB channels are determined by the charge and the size of the amino acid residues inside the central constrction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the size and charge of amino acids inside the LamB channel are the main determinants of ion selectivity and ion permeability.
the single-channel conductances of the mutant channels are not only dependent on their charge but also on their size and hydrophobicity.
the single-channel conductances of LamB mutants are strongly affected by the size of the introduced amino acid, whereas the hydrophobicity and the charge have a smaller effect.
